notes: Nothing you will see, and that is the point of this one. The app now records which country's statutory rules a set of books is kept under, and each Ghana-specific arrangement — the withholding-VAT agency rules, the community fund, the tourism levy, three-tier pensions, and the returns filed with the GRA and SSNIT — is DECLARED rather than assumed. Until now those things were simply always true. That was correct for you and it stays correct: your books are Ghana, Ghana declares every one of those arrangements, and every screen, rate, return and figure behaves exactly as it did before. The tests that matter most in this release are the ones proving that. Why do it at all: it is the groundwork for supporting a business in another country without disturbing yours. That country is not built and will not be until a real customer's own filing forms are on the table — rates can be configured, but statutory returns are forms an authority accepts, and guessing at them produces something that has to be redone the day someone files with it. One small thing follows: changing the country of an existing set of books is not offered, and never will be — books kept under one country's rules, with its returns and its chart, are not converted by a setting. No posting rule, no report, no figure changed.
